To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the diffusion MR signal can be efficiently and robustly approximated with the proposed variational framework.

(i) We propose a new method for the computation of the displacement probability density functions (PDF) from diffusion MRI data; (ii) The method is based on the approximation of the diffusion signal by a series of Laguerre-Gaussian and Spherical Harmonic functions; (iii) The estimation of the PDF is formulated as a variational problem leading to a robust estimation in the presence of noise; (iv) The method is validated on both synthetic data and real acquisitions; (v)
we present a robust method to estimate various features of the displacement PDF from the diffusion MR signal.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a new approach for diffusion MR signal analysis.
the estimation of features of the local micro-architecture of tissues from the signal measured by a diffusion MR scanner.
the development of efficient and robust tools for diffusion MR signal analysis.

the proposed method allows the estimation of a large variety of PDF-based features with high accuracy, robustness to RICIAN noise and a low computation time.
